intro.title: Hart County Roads Department
intro.description: Maintaining official county roads, rights of way, drainage, signs, bridges, pipes, and other transportation infrastructure throughout Hart County.

emergency.text: For after-hours or weekend emergency road calls, contact EMS Dispatch at

work_orders: To report a problem with a county road, including potholes, rough gravel roads, missing signs, or flooding, call the Roads Department. The County will prepare a work order and, when needed, investigate and correct the problem.
For non-emergency road work or general contact at any time, email the Roads Department.
maintenance: The Roads Department routinely maintains county roads, correcting potholes, drainage problems, missing signs, and similar issues.
Gravel roads receive routine scheduled maintenance, currently twice per year. Special projects may include paving and replacing pipes, bridges, or road sections.
Major-project schedules are proposed calendars. The current month is the most accurate; future months may change.
road_inventory: The Roads Department may work only on official county roads and within county road rights of way.
Hart County adopted its first official county road inventory in late 2002. The inventory identifies official county roads, known rights of way, road lengths, and related information.
Additions, deletions, or changes in official county-road length require a formal resolution of the Hart County Board of Commissioners.
mowing: Hart County performs bush hogging and mowing along county roads and rights of way. Work generally includes two or three cuts per year, beginning in April and ending in October.
Tree limbs are also cut back each year as needed.
long_range_plan: Hart County adopted a long-range plan based on analysis of county road assets to help prioritize limited resources and address several million dollars in deferred maintenance.
The plan began implementation in 2003 with an initial focus on sealing paved roads and resurfacing tar-and-gravel roads. Later work focused on bridges, pipes, and continued resurfacing.
The plan also contains condition ratings for paved roads that may be used to help determine resurfacing priorities. This description reflects the historical plan information published by Hart County.
